# agent-platform library chart

`charts/agent-platform` is a Helm **library chart**: the templates every agent platform deployment shares (admin, agent provisioning, chat, voice, networking, cert-manager, bundled PostgreSQL, NOTES). It has `type: library`, so it renders nothing on its own. A consumer chart (for example the Shipwright chart) depends on it and includes the templates it wants from one-line stub files. The per-helper reference lives in the [chart README](../charts/agent-platform/README.md); this page covers the contract consumers rely on.

## Where it is published

CI publishes the chart to a GitHub Pages Helm repository (the `gh-pages` branch) with `.github/workflows/chart-release.yml`:

```bash
helm repo add app-vitals https://app-vitals.github.io/agent
helm search repo app-vitals/agent-platform --versions
```

Pull requests that touch `charts/agent-platform/**` run the same lint, package and index-merge steps as a dry run, without publishing.

## Consuming it

Declare the dependency in the consumer's `Chart.yaml`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  - name: agent-platform
    version: 0.4.0
    repository: https://app-vitals.github.io/agent
```

Then add one stub file per manifest. Each stub only includes the library template, so the rendered names, labels and annotations come from the library:

```yaml
# templates/admin-deployment.yaml
{{ include "agent-platform.admin.deployment" . }}
```

Templates read the consumer's `.Values`, so the consumer's `values.yaml` must define the keys they use (`admin`, `auth`, `agent`, `chat`, `postgresql`, `networking`, ...). `tests/fixtures/consumer` in the chart directory is a complete working example.

## Extension lists

Some templates (`httproute`, `ingress`, `ingressTraefikMiddleware`, `healthcheckpolicy`, `tenantNetworkPolicy`, `postgresql.initdbConfigMap`, `notes`) interleave platform services with services only the consumer knows about. The consumer passes its own entries as a dict argument rather than through `.Values`, because entries often depend on consumer conditions:

```yaml
# templates/httproute.yaml
{{ include "agent-platform.httproute" (dict "context" . "extensions" (include "myapp.platformExtensions" . | fromYaml)) }}
```

`myapp.platformExtensions` is a named template in the consumer that renders YAML with any of these optional keys:

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `routes` | An HTTPRoute and Ingress path per entry (`component`, `pathPrefix`, `port`, optional `name` and `stripPrefix`), ahead of the admin `/` catch-all |
| `healthChecks` | A GKE HealthCheckPolicy per entry (`component`, optional `requestPath`), after admin's |
| `networkPolicyEgress` | Same-namespace egress peers (`component`) in the tenant NetworkPolicy |
| `databases` | `CREATE DATABASE` scripts (`file`, `name`) in the bundled PostgreSQL init ConfigMap, before chat's |
| `notes` | NOTES.txt banner `productName`, `servicePorts` and free-text `sections` |

Calling a template with the bare root context (`{{ include "agent-platform.httproute" . }}`) renders the platform-only set, with no extensions. The full key shapes are in the [chart README](../charts/agent-platform/README.md#extension-lists).

## Versioning

The chart `version` tracks the platform release. When a release changes the shared templates, bump `version` in `charts/agent-platform/Chart.yaml` to the release's `X.Y.Z`. Merging the bump to `main` publishes that version, and the workflow then sends a `chart-release` dispatch carrying the version to `app-vitals/shipwright` so it can bump its dependency. An unchanged version repackages to no diff, so nothing new is published without a bump. Consumers pin an exact version and upgrade on their own schedule.

## Stable names

The library renders the same resource names, selector labels and Service names its consumers already run in clusters, so adopting or upgrading the library must not change them. Treat these as a compatibility surface:

- Do not rename a resource, a named template or a Service, or change a selector label, without a deliberate migration. Selectors on existing Deployments are immutable, and other systems reach some Services by name (the chat Service is reached through an ExternalName alias).
- The persisted admin Secret keeps its generated keys across `helm upgrade` by looking up the installed Secret; do not change its name or keys.
- Named templates live under the `agent-platform.` namespace. Renaming one breaks every consumer stub that includes it, so add a new template and deprecate the old one instead.

The fixture consumer's tests assert the rendered output, so an accidental rename fails them. Run them with:

```bash
helm plugin install https://github.com/helm-unittest/helm-unittest
helm dependency build charts/agent-platform/tests/fixtures/consumer
helm unittest charts/agent-platform/tests/fixtures/consumer
```
